path = "data_small/"
def FeatureExtractor(path, n_mels, fmax=20000, fmin=20):

    data = []

    for dirname, _, filenames in os.walk(path):
        for filename in filenames:
            full_path = os.path.join(dirname, filename)

            y, sr = librosa.load(full_path)
            mel = librosa.feature.melspectrogram(y=y, sr=sr, n_mels=n_mels, fmax=fmax, fmin=fmin)
            logam = librosa.power_to_db(mel)
            # Reduce variable-length time axis to fixed-size feature vector
            feat = np.mean(logam, axis=1)
            data.append(feat)

    data = np.array(data)
    return data

def run_model(model, dataloader, optimizer, train=True):
    if train:
        model.train()
    else:
        model.eval()

    pred = []
    True_labels = []

    # CrossEntropyLoss expects class indices (LongTensor), not one-hot vectors
    ce_loss = torch.nn.CrossEntropyLoss()

    total_loss = 0.0
    for (data, label) in dataloader:
        data = data.to(device).float()
        label = label.to(device).float()

        if train:
            optimizer.zero_grad()

        output, out_aux = model(data)

        # Convert one-hot labels to class indices for CE loss
        target_idx = torch.argmax(label, dim=1).long()

        loss_main = ce_loss(output, target_idx)

        # aux head has 6294 outputs in this model setup, so same target indices apply
        loss_aux = ce_loss(out_aux, target_idx)

        mod_loss = loss_main + loss_aux

        if train:
            mod_loss.backward()
            optimizer.step()

        total_loss += mod_loss.item()
        pred.append(output.detach())
        True_labels.append(label.detach())

    return pred, True_labels, total_loss / len(dataloader)

            mel = librosa.feature.melspectrogram(y=y, sr=sr, n_mels=n_mels, fmax=fmax, fmin=fmin)

            # Make all samples same length so they can be stacked into a NumPy array

    data = np.array(data)

class History(Callback):
    def __init__(self, model, validation_images, validation_labels):
        self.model_ = model
        self.validation_images = validation_images
        self.validation_labels = validation_labels
        self.accuracy = [0]
        self.loss = [5]
        self.val_accuracy = [0]

        scores = self.model_.evaluate(
            self.validation_images,
            self.validation_labels,
            verbose=0
        )
        print('\n', scores, '\n')
        self.loss.append(logs.get('loss'))
        self.accuracy.append(logs.get('accuracy'))
        self.val_loss.append(scores[0])
        self.val_accuracy.append(scores[1])

    opt = SGD(learning_rate)
    model.compile(optimizer=opt, loss='categorical_crossentropy', metrics=['accuracy'])

    model.fit(

        batch_size=batch_size,
        epochs=num_epochs,

    total_loss = 0
    for (data, label) in dataloader:

def run_model(model, dataloader, optimizer, train=True):
    if train:
        model.train()
    else:
        model.eval()

    pred = []
    True_labels = []

    # Keep CE loss, but convert one-hot labels to class indices
    ce_loss = torch.nn.CrossEntropyLoss()
    # Auxiliary head outputs 6294 classes as defined in the model
    aux_loss_fn = torch.nn.CrossEntropyLoss()

    total_loss = 0.0
    for (data, label) in dataloader:
        data = data.to(device).float()
        label = label.to(device).float()

        # CrossEntropyLoss expects class indices of shape [N]
        target_idx = torch.argmax(label, dim=1).long()

        optimizer.zero_grad()
        output, out_aux = model(data)

        output = output.float()
        out_aux = out_aux.float()

        loss_main = ce_loss(output, target_idx)
        loss_aux = aux_loss_fn(out_aux, target_idx)
        mod_loss = loss_main + loss_aux

        if train:
            mod_loss.backward()
            optimizer.step()

        total_loss += mod_loss.item()
        pred.append(output.detach())
        True_labels.append(label.detach())

    return pred, True_labels, total_loss / len(dataloader)
